answer: Cross-epoch trajectory matching. Each identity must file a signed route of task transitions per epoch; the protocol verifies that consecutive epochs connect into one continuous behavioural voyage, checking overlap of collaborators, timing, and outcome distributions. A karst of synthetic identities fails because cloned agents replay identical paths and drift apart under perturbation. Genuine histories form a branching trellis that is costly to fabricate: an attacker must run each puppet through distinct, plausible work for multiple epochs before it counts,
